title.zh: 讓量子電腦學會「從錯誤中學習」：強化學習打造永不當機的量子校正器
title.en: Teaching Quantum Computers to Learn From Their Mistakes: Reinforcement Learning for Continuous Error Correction

summary.zh:
【總結】量子電腦極度脆弱，需要透過量子誤差校正（QEC）來保護。然而，維持QEC效能需要持續微調上千個控制參數——傳統做法是暫停整個計算來重新校準，但這與未來需要連續運算數天甚至數月的演算法根本不相容。研究團隊提出了一個嶄新範式：將QEC的誤差檢測事件轉化為強化學習訊號，讓AI代理在計算過程中同時學習並校正系統。這項研究在Willow超導處理器上成功實現，將邏輯穩定性提升3.5倍，並創下表面碼與顏色碼的紀錄級表現，開啟了「從錯誤中學習、永不當機」的量子計算新紀元。

【研究問題】量子電腦本質上是類比機器，極易受環境擾動影響。雖然QEC能將錯誤「數位化」為可檢測的訊號並進行糾錯，但QEC有效運作的前提是物理閘錯誤率必須遠低於閾值（約10⁻³至10⁻²）。問題在於，控制參數會隨時間漂移，而過去所有實驗都依賴「暫停計算→重新校準→恢復計算」的循環，這種斷断续續的模式在面對需要連續執行數天至數月的未來量子演算法時，將成為無法克服的瓶頸。

【研究方法】研究團隊在Willow超導處理器上實施了一套強化學習框架。他們在距離5和7的表面碼、以及距離5的顏色碼上執行量子記憶演算法，由RL代理同時管理超過1,000個控制參數。核心思路是：在計算過程中對所有控制參數施加微小擾動，觀察誤差檢測事件率的變化，從而建立參數變動與系統表現之間的因果關係。他們構建了一個代理目標函數——誤差檢測事件率，並利用檢測區域的局部性（每個探測器僅與約302個參數相關聯），透過因素圖結構實現高效的高維度優化。學習演算法採用多目標策略梯度方法，每輪從政策分佈中抽樣一批候選政策，根據誤差檢測率評分，再計算梯度更新政策分佈。

【結果】研究團隊取得了多項突破性成果：RL微調在傳統校準基礎上進一步將邏輯誤差率（LER）降低了20%；距離7表面碼達到了7.72(9)×10⁻⁴的創紀錄LER（當時所有物理量子比特模態中的最佳紀錄），距離5顏色碼達到8.19(14)×10⁻³。在人工注入漂移的測試中，RL控制將邏輯穩定性提升了2.4倍，加入解碼器協同控制後更達3.5倍提升。數值模擬進一步驗證了可擴展性——在距離15表面碼（約40,000個控制參數）上，收斂速度與系統大小無關，證明該方法可無縫擴展至未來大規模量子處理器。
summary.en:
**Summary:** Quantum computers are inherently fragile analogue machines that require quantum error correction (QEC) to function. Yet keeping QEC effective demands continuous calibration of thousands of control parameters—a task that has historically required halting computation entirely. This paper introduces a paradigm-shifting solution: repurposing QEC's own error-detection events as a learning signal for a reinforcement learning agent that steers control parameters in real time, without ever stopping the computation. Demonstrated on Google's Willow superconducting processor, the approach improves logical stability 3.5-fold under injected drift and sets new records for surface and colour codes, charting a path toward quantum computers that learn from their errors and never stop computing.

**Problem:** Quantum error correction can only work if physical gate error rates stay well below a threshold of roughly 10⁻³ to 10⁻². But the analogue control parameters governing qubit operations drift over time due to environmental noise, temperature fluctuations, and other instabilities. Every prior experiment solved this by pausing computation for recalibration—an approach fundamentally incompatible with the long-running algorithms (days to months) needed for practical applications like factoring large integers or simulating molecular reactions. The field needed a way to calibrate continuously, without interrupting the computation.

**Approach:** The researchers deployed a reinforcement learning agent on distance-5 and distance-7 surface codes and a distance-5 colour code running on Willow's superconducting processor. The agent manages over 1,000 control parameters that translate abstract QEC circuits into physical microwave pulses. Instead of optimizing the logical error rate directly—which would require an impractically large number of cycles—the team constructed a surrogate objective: the average rate of error-detection events. This objective is efficiently computable and, crucially, its components depend sparsely on the control parameters due to the locality of detecting regions in the QEC circuit. This sparsity is captured in a factor graph, where each detector connects only to the parameters of gates in its detecting region (averaging 302 parameters per detector in the distance-5 experiment). The agent uses a multi-objective policy-gradient RL algorithm with entropy regularization to maintain exploration, iteratively sampling policy candidates, ranking them by detection-event rate, and updating the policy distribution via gradient steps.

**Results:** The RL fine-tuning yielded a consistent 20% additional suppression of the logical error rate beyond what traditional calibration and human expertise could achieve. The distance-7 surface code reached a record LER of 7.72(9)×10⁻⁴—the best performance demonstrated across any physical qubit modality to date—while the distance-5 colour code achieved 8.19(14)×10⁻³. Under artificially injected drift, RL steering improved logical stability 2.4-fold (3.5-fold when combined with decoder steering), with a characteristic response time of approximately 130 epochs. Numerical simulations of a distance-15 surface code with ~40,000 control parameters confirmed that the convergence rate is independent of system size, establishing the framework's scalability. The work demonstrates that a quantum computer can learn from its errors in real time, eliminating the need for disruptive recalibration pauses.

keyArticle.title: Reinforcement learning control of quantum error correction
